subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, and operators?
rationale: The current code has Gateway event primitives that could support observation, but exposing cross-channel transcripts changes product scope, security expectations, and likely public CLI/config surface.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that shows only authorized activity for the selected agent/session scope and defers bidirectional mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces, but require explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No core mirror mode
options.body: Keep raw logs, session tailing, or a future activity timeline as the supported monitoring path and avoid a core cross-channel TUI mirror feature.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that shows only authorized activity for the selected agent/session scope and defers bidirectional mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest routing candidate from the related TUI session isolation and live-update history, and the decision is a product/security boundary rather than a narrow code repair.
